control.basis: Raise the hood 8 mm, inside a plausible fabrication error, so its lip enters the undeformed FUEL path at the pinch

objectives.objective: AUTO: start with up to eight supported FUEL and score from a legal launch pose while the HUB is active
objectives.basis: The starting fold holds 36 or more FUEL by free volume (start-capacity premise); launch-wrap and flight cases carry a FUEL into the HUB opening from the 2.7 m pose that the re-run rehearsal credits in AUTO (delivery-pose premise). Delivering from 2.70 m instead of 2.16 m costs 8 FUEL over the three rehearsed matches (96 against 104).

objectives.objective: Inactive shift: collect and hold the next allocated stock from the DEPOT, OUTPOST or a partner
objectives.basis: acquire-* cases take a floor FUEL up the bumper face into the hopper; the acquisition physics trial captures it in 0.50 s; hopper-capacity is 36 or more by free volume.

objectives.objective: Active shift: carry each FUEL from storage through one transfer into the HUB
objectives.basis: loaded-transit, index, launch-wrap and flight cases carry the tracked FUEL into the HUB cavity; the delivery physics trial scores from 6.70 to 7.10 m/s.

objectives.objective: Active shift: sustain 2.00 FUEL/s to score 24 with stock ready by second 5
objectives.basis: Two pinch lanes; by calculation each lane feeds 3.9 FUEL/s at 0.6 m/s belt speed and 154 mm spacing, and the flywheel recovers a 2% speed drop in about 0.03 s on two motors, so the layout supplies 7.8 FUEL/s against 2.00. Bulk convergence without jams is gate G1. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: Fallback: score the available batch when supply or traffic consumes the window and return to collecting
objectives.basis: The cycle is piece-count independent; the intake stays deployed in every operating case; the re-run rehearsal keeps the depot loop.

objectives.objective: Traffic: remain in the own zone, keep possession through loaded driving and contact, and yield
objectives.basis: By geometry the front lip stands 77 mm above a floor FUEL's base, more than its 75 mm radius, so horizontal deceleration alone cannot roll it out; side and rear walls rise above the top layer; the open throat holds no counted FUEL. Loaded 0.5 g stops are gate G2. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: Neutral collector alternative with two field crossings
objectives.basis: The coordinator selected the own-zone role. R3 keeps a BUMP crossing option (bump-crossing premise, 8.7 mm least clearance) with the intake retracted; the re-run TRENCH variant (R3L) credits fewer FUEL than the depot loop.

objectives.objective: End game: Level 1 low-rung hang when its expected 10 points exceed the remaining FUEL service
objectives.basis: Cases reach, seat (2 mm required contact) and lift 70 mm; the 714 mm frame gives 23.9 mm of bumper overlap with each upright (hang-bumper-overlap premise); the hang physics trial holds 37.8 mm with the brake and fails without it. Jaw capture under lateral offset and the brake hold are gate G3. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: AUTO Level 1 TOWER (15 points, two-robot cap)
objectives.basis: The strategy keeps the eight-FUEL AUTO objective; no joined AUTO climb evidence is sought in this layout.

objectives.objective: Reserve the depot entrance and partner lane
objectives.basis: Alliance routing decision owned by the field rehearsal, independent of the robot layout.

objectives.objective: Measurement: observe intake crossing, retained identity, release and downstream crossing on one timebase
objectives.basis: entry sensor at the front lip and pinch sensor at the flywheel lane are placed; the HUB counter is field equipment.

frame rail front.rationale: The foundation's 680 mm length and module saddles carry forward; the frame widens to 714 mm (2788 mm perimeter) for hang overlap, so the side-rail saddle fits must be redrawn.

floor pan.rationale: Sits 94 mm above the carpet; the BUMP crossing screen then leaves 24 mm at the belly and 8.7 mm at the front bumper corner.

front lip.purpose: Keep floor-level FUEL from rolling out over the front rail.
front lip.rationale: Its 170 mm top stands 2 mm above the floor-layer centres and 5 mm below the entering FUEL.

intake slide rail left.purpose: Guide the intake carriage between the start fold and the pickup pose.
intake slide rail left.rationale: A straight slide never sweeps beyond the 304.8 mm R105 reach; the fixed stage of the two-stage slide is drawn.

intake slide rail right.purpose: Guide the intake carriage between the start fold and the pickup pose.
intake slide rail right.rationale: A straight slide never sweeps beyond the 304.8 mm R105 reach; the fixed stage of the two-stage slide is drawn.

bumper front.rationale: The 48-168 mm zone and 76 mm section follow the foundation release; the front bumper face is the pinch backing, and its 866.15 mm width overlaps each TOWER upright by 23.9 mm.

bumper rear.rationale: The 48-168 mm zone and 76 mm section follow the foundation release; the front bumper face is the pinch backing, and its 866.15 mm width overlaps each TOWER upright by 23.9 mm.

hopper wall left.purpose: Contain stacked FUEL up to 715 mm.
hopper wall left.rationale: Walls rise 85 mm above the top-layer centres so a stable stack stays inside.

hopper wall right.purpose: Contain stacked FUEL up to 715 mm.
hopper wall right.rationale: Walls rise 85 mm above the top-layer centres so a stable stack stays inside.

hopper front upper wall.purpose: Close the hopper front above the intake throat.
hopper front upper wall.rationale: It starts at 482 mm, above the slide's swept path and the stowed carriage.

hopper rear wall.purpose: Separate stored FUEL from the spinning flywheel.
hopper rear wall.rationale: Only the floor-level lane may reach the pinch; upper layers would double-feed or jam on the wheel top.

floor belt main.purpose: Move the bottom FUEL layer aft toward the flywheel pinch.
floor belt main.rationale: Feeding straight from the floor removes the incumbent's vertical elevator transfer.

floor belt front.purpose: Move the bottom FUEL layer aft toward the flywheel pinch.
floor belt front.rationale: Feeding straight from the floor removes the incumbent's vertical elevator transfer.

indexer cleat.purpose: Push one tracked FUEL along the floor lane into the pinch.
indexer cleat.rationale: A cleated belt gives a positive drive path that a free-piece test can meter.

flywheel.purpose: Accelerate the FUEL against the hood.
flywheel.rationale: A 4 in floor-fed flywheel at 62 degrees enters from 2.4 to 3.6 m under every drag and spin corner; 0.006 kg m2 limits the speed drop per shot to about 1.6-2%.

hood.purpose: Guide the FUEL 62 degrees around the flywheel and release it at 62 degrees elevation.
hood.rationale: Its end stops 2 mm inside the rear perimeter, so the shooter never extends a second side.

shooter side plate left.purpose: Carry the flywheel bearings and hood.
shooter side plate left.rationale: Plates stop 4 mm short of the rear modules and bound the two pinch lanes.

shooter side plate right.purpose: Carry the flywheel bearings and hood.
shooter side plate right.rationale: Plates stop 4 mm short of the rear modules and bound the two pinch lanes.

flywheel motor left.purpose: Drive the flywheel from both ends.
flywheel motor left.rationale: Outboard of each side plate, clear of the battery, the panels and the rear modules.

flywheel motor right.purpose: Drive the flywheel from both ends.
flywheel motor right.rationale: Outboard of each side plate, clear of the battery, the panels and the rear modules.

battery.rationale: Standing on its end at the left side lets it lift straight out between the hook arm and rear wall.

electronics panel.purpose: Hold power distribution, controller, radio, breaker and 15 motor controllers on both faces.
electronics panel.rationale: The side strips are outside the floor lanes and reachable from above.

electronics panel left.purpose: Hold power distribution, controller, radio, breaker and 15 motor controllers on both faces.
electronics panel left.rationale: The side strips are outside the floor lanes and reachable from above.

entry sensor.purpose: Observe each FUEL crossing the intake lip.
entry sensor.rationale: The strategy requires per-piece intake crossings on the match timebase.

pinch sensor.purpose: Observe each FUEL entering the flywheel lane.
pinch sensor.rationale: Separates retained identity from release for the counting requirement.

climber tube left.rationale: Front corners above the modules give a straight load path into the frame for the hang.

climber tube right.rationale: Front corners above the modules give a straight load path into the frame for the hang.

climber winch.purpose: Retract both inner tubes by cable to lift the robot.
climber winch.rationale: One motor at the front top keeps both hooks synchronized; it must hold 625 N with power removed (F4).

climber inner tube left.purpose: Telescope inside the outer tube to seat the hook and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber inner tube left.rationale: A round tube lets the hook swing on top without the tube rotating in its guide; the swing actuator sits inside it.

climber inner tube right.purpose: Telescope inside the outer tube to seat the hook and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber inner tube right.rationale: A round tube lets the hook swing on top without the tube rotating in its guide; the swing actuator sits inside it.

climber hook left.purpose: Swing over the low rung, seat and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber hook left.rationale: Stowed inside the perimeter for R106; a 180 degree inboard swing avoids a second-side extension.

climber hook right.purpose: Swing over the low rung, seat and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber hook right.rationale: Stowed inside the perimeter for R106; a 180 degree inboard swing avoids a second-side extension.

intake belt module.purpose: Lift a floor FUEL up the bumper face.
intake belt module.rationale: A vertical belt 3 mm off the undeformed FUEL pinches it against the bumper inside the 304.8 mm reach; compression is a detailed-design setting.

intake top roller.purpose: Push the lifted FUEL aft over the bumper.
intake top roller.rationale: Placed 3 mm above the FUEL at the top of the climb.
intake top roller.material: 2 in compliant wheels on hex shaft

intake carriage plate left.purpose: Join the belt module and top roller to the slide.
intake carriage plate left.rationale: Plates at 262-272 mm pass between the 819 mm TOWER uprights so the intake can stay deployed during the climb.

intake carriage plate right.purpose: Join the belt module and top roller to the slide.
intake carriage plate right.rationale: Plates at 262-272 mm pass between the 819 mm TOWER uprights so the intake can stay deployed during the climb.

FUEL tracked.purpose: Follow one identifiable FUEL from the carpet into the HUB.
FUEL tracked.rationale: Its undeformed path carries the custody, clearance and ballistic checks.

FUEL stored 1.purpose: Represent stored stock in the starting fold.
FUEL stored 1.rationale: Supported pockets from the deposition screen that stay clear of every commissioned path; capacity itself is the free-volume premise.

FUEL stored 2.purpose: Represent stored stock in the starting fold.
FUEL stored 2.rationale: Supported pockets from the deposition screen that stay clear of every commissioned path; capacity itself is the free-volume premise.

hub body.purpose: Locate the HUB and its hexagonal opening.
hub body.rationale: The flight cases must clear the near flat at 1828.8 mm and descend inside the conservative inscribed opening.

hub top.purpose: Locate the HUB and its hexagonal opening.
hub top.rationale: The flight cases must clear the near flat at 1828.8 mm and descend inside the conservative inscribed opening.

tower upright left.rationale: Their 819 mm gap bounds the intake and the bumper approach.

tower upright right.rationale: Their 819 mm gap bounds the intake and the bumper approach.

tower low rung.purpose: Locate the low rung at 685.8 mm.
tower low rung.rationale: The hooks must seat on it; the V0 text centres it in the upright depth.

tower base.rationale: Level 1 requires clearing it; its 8 mm edge stands under the front bumper at the berth.
